docRequirement: claude-directory.md catalogues `.worktreeinclude` as a first-class project-scope config file and binds three things about it. WHERE: "Lives at the project root, not inside `.claude/`" (:89 tips), repeated in the file-reference prose "Project-scope files live in your repo under `.claude/` (or at the root for `CLAUDE.md`, `.mcp.json`, and `.worktreeinclude`)" (:1476) and in the table row `.worktreeinclude` | Project only | commit ✓ | "Gitignored files to copy into new worktrees" (:1497). WHEN: "Read when Claude creates a git worktree via `--worktree`, the `EnterWorktree` tool, or subagent `isolation: worktree`" (:87), plus "Also applies to parallel sessions in the desktop app" (:89). WHAT: "Lists gitignored files to copy from your main repository into each new worktree. Worktrees are fresh checkouts, so untracked files like `.env` are missing by default. Patterns here use `.gitignore` syntax. Only files that match a pattern and are also gitignored get copied, so tracked files are never duplicated." (:88), with the documented example being comment- and blank-line-tolerant (`# Local environment` / `.env` / `.env.local` / `config/secrets.json`). One carve-out: "Git-only: if you configure a WorktreeCreate hook for a different VCS, this file is not read. Copy files inside your hook script instead" (:89).
current: Nothing in the fork ever opens the file. `grep -rain -l worktreeinclude packages apps scripts` matches only the bundled third-party binary `apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/darwin-arm64/codex-app-server` (and its `dist/` copy) — zero TypeScript hits; positive control on the same rig: the same grep for `symlinkDirectories` hits packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts and three more. The whole creation path is closed: `WorktreeLeaseService.acquireUnlocked` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:207-234) selects a path, offers it to a `WorktreeCreate` hook (:220 → :251-284 `applyWorktreeCreateHookPath`), then calls `this.options.git.create(...)` (:227). The one production implementation of `git.create` is packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10164-10198: `show-ref` for branch existence (:10166-10171), then every command from `worktreeCreateCommands` (:10176-10185 → packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96, which emits only `worktree add` [+ `--no-checkout`], `sparse-checkout set --cone`, `checkout`), then the links from `worktreeSymlinkPlan` (:10189-10197 → worktree-git-plan.ts:112-124, `symlinkDirectories` only, `symlink()` not `copyFile()`, missing target skipped). No `readFile`, no gitignore parsing, no copy anywhere on that path. The project root the page names IS available at that exact point — `projectRoot()` at SessionManager.ts:10113 resolves `(await worktreeAuthority()).root` (:10099-10112), the canonical project handle path — so the file's location is not the obstacle. Both entry points we ship converge on that same closure: `EnterWorktree` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts:19-44, `ctx.worktree.enter` at :32 → SessionManager.ts:10238-10307, `leases.acquire` at :10269) and subagent `isolation: worktree` (parsed at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:348-351 JSON form and :635-639 frontmatter form → SessionManager.ts:10334-10347 `acquirePiWorktreeLease`). There is no settings-level substitute either: packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:60 admits exactly `baseRef`/`symlinkDirectories`/`sparsePaths`/`bgIsolation` and `assertKnownKeys` (:78-83) THROWS `invalid worktree setting: <key>` on anything else, with both list defaults empty (:71-76). The `--worktree` CLI entry point named at :87 does not exist in this fork at all (`grep -ran -- --worktree apps/cli/src packages/server/src packages/server-core/src` → one comment in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-orphan-sweep.test.ts:185), so only two of the page's three triggers are even reachable.
divergence: The mechanism is entirely absent — not a wrong key name, not a narrower glob, not a misspelled field. No code reads `<projectRoot>/.worktreeinclude`, nothing parses `.gitignore` syntax for it, nothing asks git which paths are ignored, and no file of any kind is copied into a worktree. What claude-directory.md files as a committed, project-root config file simply has no reader, so the file is inert if a user writes it — and because it is not a settings key, it fails silently rather than erroring (writing the equivalent under `worktree.*` in settings.json errors instead, at worktree-settings.ts:81). The two adjacent mechanisms we do ship are not it and must not be mistaken for it: (a) `worktree.symlinkDirectories` (worktree-git-plan.ts:112-124) SYMLINKS instead of copying, takes plain repo-relative paths rather than gitignore patterns, has no "and is also gitignored" filter, and defaults empty — different semantics (writes inside the worktree write through to the main checkout); (b) the `WorktreeCreate` command hook we ship (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360, :394, path capture at :1247-1259) is exactly what the page's tip offers INSTEAD of `.worktreeinclude`, not an implementation of it. Second-order delta on the carve-out: our `WorktreeCreate` hook replaces only the PATH (worktree-lease-service.ts:251-284) and `git.create` still runs afterwards, so "a hook is configured ⇒ this file is not read" has no flag to hang off today. Scope note: this is the `.claude`-directory view of one gap that three pages state — f096 (worktrees.md) and f159 (desktop.md) are the same missing reader. ONE fix, three pages; f096 carries the same edit list.

change.what: New pure planner, sibling to worktree-git-plan.ts and in the same 'assertable without a repository, a supervisor and a session' shape that file's header states. (1) `parseWorktreeInclude(text: string)` — gitignore syntax per the page's example: drop blank lines and `#` comments (`\#` escapes a literal `#`), trim unescaped trailing whitespace, record `negated` for a leading `!`, `anchored` for a leading `/`, `directoryOnly` for a trailing `/`. Reuse the entry/length caps from packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:64-65 (128/512) and refuse absolute forms and `..` segments exactly as `repoRelativePaths` does (:91-107) — a project-root file must not be able to name a source outside the repository. (2) `worktreeIncludeCandidateCommands(repoRoot)` → `WorktreeGitCommand[]` (the interface at worktree-git-plan.ts:16-23) producing the authoritative candidate set from git itself: `['-C', repoRoot, 'ls-files', '-z', '--others', '--ignored', '--exclude-standard', '--directory', '--no-empty-directory']`, operation `include-list`, cwd `'repo'`, `allowFailure: true`; `--directory --no-empty-directory` is what stops a repo with `node_modules` emitting 200k paths, and for each wildcard-free pattern also emit a targeted `['-C', repoRoot, 'check-ignore', '-q', '--', <pattern>]` so a file inside a collapsed ignored directory stays reachable. Using git as the ignore oracle is what satisfies the page's 'and are also gitignored' clause without a second ignore implementation. (3) `worktreeIncludePlan({ repoRoot, worktreePath, patterns, ignoredEntries })` → `{ source, destination }[]`, applying gitignore's last-matching-pattern-wins with negation and joining against the resolved roots so a destination can only land inside the worktree (same containment argument as worktree-git-plan.ts:105-111).

The single fix point — all three product entry points inherit it. Insert the include step AFTER the `worktreeCreateCommands` loop (:10185, so a sparse checkout has materialised) and next to the existing symlink loop (:10189-10197): read `<root>/.worktreeinclude` where `root = await projectRoot()` (:10113) — the PROJECT root the page names, unprefixed, NOT the worktree and NOT `.nessy-agent/`, so the de-brand does not rename it. Absent file ⇒ no-op. Run the candidate commands through the existing `runGit` (:10117-10133; its containment root and `additionalWritableRoots: [root, namespaceRoot]` already cover this), feed the output to `worktreeIncludePlan`, then per pair `mkdir(dirname(destination), { recursive: true })` + `copyFile(source, destination)` and `chmod` to the source's mode — these are secrets, a `.env` at 0600 must not land 0644 — skipping when the destination already exists. Failure tolerance must copy the symlink precedent immediately below (`sessionLog.warn`, never fail creation), including a malformed `.worktreeinclude`. Skip-if-exists is load-bearing, not politeness: `recoverUnlocked` re-invokes `git.create` for a `creating` lease (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:296), so the step must be idempotent.

Small plumbing for the page's Git-only carve-out (:89). Have `applyWorktreeCreateHookPath` (:251-284) additionally report whether it adopted a hook-returned path, and widen `create(lease: WorktreeLeaseV1)` to `create(lease, context: { hookReplacedPath: boolean })`; SessionManager's implementation skips the include step when it is true. Pass it as a CALL ARGUMENT, never as a field on `WorktreeLeaseV1` — that type is persisted (`managed.worktreeLeaseState`, schemaVersion 1, persisted at SessionManager.ts:10137-10142), and adding a field there converts an M into a persistence-boundary change for no gain. The `recoverUnlocked` call site passes `{ hookReplacedPath: false }`.

Table-driven over parser + plan, no repository needed. Cases: the page's own example (`# Local environment` / `.env` / `.env.local` / blank / `# API credentials` / `config/secrets.json`) yields exactly those three copies and ignores both comments and the blank line; a negation (`.env*` then `!.env.production`) excludes the last; a path that matches a pattern but is ABSENT from the ignored-entries set is not copied (the 'tracked files are never duplicated' clause); `..`, an absolute entry and an over-length entry are refused; a pattern matching an entry collapsed to `node_modules/` does not expand into the directory. Put candidate-command assertions in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts only if the commands land in that module instead.

Explicit non-change, because extending it is the obvious wrong move. It is the PERMISSION matcher: its header pins it to permissions.md's documented subset ('Character classes are NOT documented rule syntax', :5-6) and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/permission-dsl.ts:6 is its consumer. Reuse it read-only for the per-segment glob core inside the new planner and keep `!`/leading-`/`/trailing-`/` local to worktree-include-plan.ts. Likewise do NOT add a key to packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts — `.worktreeinclude` is a project-root file, not a settings key, and that parser throws on unknown keys by design (:78-83).

blastRadius: Confined to packages/server-core plus one read-only import from packages/shared. `git.create` has exactly one production implementation (SessionManager.ts:10164) and two call sites (worktree-lease-service.ts:227 acquire, :296 recover), so widening its signature touches the fake `git` ports in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.test.ts and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-orphan-sweep.test.ts. `worktreeCreateCommands` and `worktreeSymlinkPlan` each have 3 callers in SessionManager.ts and are covered by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts. All three of the page's reachable triggers inherit the fix without their own edit: `EnterWorktree` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts:32 → SessionManager.ts:10269), subagent `isolation: worktree` (runtime-agent-definition.ts:348-351,:635-639 → SessionManager.ts:10345), and desktop parallel sessions, which use the same session worktree port. NO wire or schema boundary is crossed provided the hook flag rides the call argument; putting it on `WorktreeLeaseV1` would cross the persisted `worktreeLeaseState` boundary (schemaVersion 1) and is rejected above. There IS a security boundary and it is the thing review must check: this becomes the first path that copies gitignored SECRETS out of the main checkout into `<dirname(projectRoot)>/.nessy-worktrees/<project>/<leaseId>/` (namespace built at SessionManager.ts:10105-10110), a directory that outlives the session until the orphan sweep removes it — and a subagent under `isolation: worktree` is precisely the actor previously denied those files. Mode preservation and destination containment are the two review gates.
userImpact: Observable today, and silent. A user whose project keeps local config in a gitignored `.env` runs a subagent with `isolation: worktree`, or the model calls `EnterWorktree`, and the worktree comes up without it: `bun run dev`, a test run, a migration or any script that reads `.env` fails inside the worktree with missing-variable errors while the identical command works in the main checkout, and nothing in the transcript says a file was not carried over. The documented remedy also fails silently — a user who follows claude-directory.md, commits `.worktreeinclude` at the project root (the page marks it committed, so it is the kind of file a team shares), and sees no error will conclude it worked; expressing the same intent as a settings key instead fails loudly with `invalid worktree setting` (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:81). The workarounds that do work are undiscoverable and semantically different: listing the path under `worktree.symlinkDirectories` yields a symlink whose edits write back into the main checkout, or the user hand-writes a `WorktreeCreate` command hook.
